provenance.title: Split the 43 large files flagged by CodeFlow
provenance.metric: patterns[Architecture Issues].architectureIssues[] (43 Large Files) — the same predicate as God Object: analyzed files where isCode !== false && functions.length > 15 (index.html detectPatterns `godFiles`). `functions` is the headless parser count mirrored by test/fixtures/function-count-mirror.mts; the ceiling is strictly greater than 15.

after.note: 20 - 1: `server.py` fell from 16 to 13 functions when its `/api/repos/*` routes moved to `handler_api.py`. The 19 survivors are the same files, so `after.count` is `deferred` + `unfiledFlagged`.

removed.reason: the Caveman mode extension was removed with its whole tree (#2072)

deferred.reason: no Rust toolchain in the pipeline image — `which cargo rustc` is empty and no workflow compiles `embedded/docker/ui`, so a `mod`-declared move cannot be checked in-gate (#2002-#2006, #2034-#2036 precedent)
deferred.requires: a cargo gate (rust:1.99-bookworm builder image) in tests.yml; until then a Rust split's "tests stay green" is unfalsifiable

deferred.reason: `fp-filter.js` is served byte-verbatim at `/fp-filter.js` and COPYed into the image as one artifact: it is a deliberate dual-consumer UMD (`<script src>` in the served page, CJS `require` in `run-analysis.mjs`), so its boundary is a delivery contract, not a module seam
deferred.requires: 3 COPY lines, 3 serve routes and a third `_BRIDGE_SCRIPT` tag to keep the split serving byte-identically — a delivery redesign, not a refactor

unfiledFlagged.reason: flagged at delivery but not filed by #2031: these are `mod`-declared siblings that earlier Rust splits (#2002-#2006, #2034-#2036) minted. They carry the same blocker as the deferred Rust group — no cargo gate — so they are recorded rather than silently dropped from the live measurement.
unfiledFlagged.requires: a cargo gate in tests.yml (same prerequisite as the deferred Rust group)

notScored.reason: `.mts` is absent from CODE_EXTS at the pinned ref, so the analyzer never scores these (yet they were filed)
scored by the analyzer and below the `> 15` ceiling at delivery — reduced by an earlier issue in this chain or never over it; each count is asserted `<= 15` by the oracle
